_comment: Hand-researched additions to the spreadsheet catalogue. Every entry here was verified by request on 2026-08-03. 'replaces' points at a dataset key whose spreadsheet link is an HTML page (or dead); 'extra' entries are live APIs the spreadsheet does not list at all but that matter for emergency response.

beach-exposure.note: Spreadsheet links the NIWA Hub page. The queryable service behind it:

coastal-inundation-index.note: The Hub page is dead - it falls back to NIWA's generic landing page and the Hub search no longer lists the inundation index. The underlying service is still live and published: This layer also carries CSI_cc (the erosion score) alongside CSI_in, and has the same 1811 segments as coastal-erosion-index - the two catalogue rows are one dataset published twice.

coastal-landform.note: Spreadsheet links the NIWA Hub page. The queryable service behind it:

coastal-erosion-index.note: The URL on the Hub landing page is an archived, broken on-prem Map Service (publishes zero layers, NaN extent, HTTP 500 on layer 0). The data is published separately as a hosted Feature Service under the NIWA_OpenData org, anonymous and CC-BY-4.0. NOTE: this single layer carries BOTH indices - CSI_cc is the coastal-change/erosion score and CSI_in the inundation score - so it is the same 1811-segment dataset as coastal-inundation-index, published twice. Either endpoint gives you both columns.
coastal-erosion-index.found_via: subagent search of the ArcGIS sharing API; independently re-verified 2026-08-03

flood-exposure-map.note: The ArcGIS webmap item is not publicly shared. Greater Wellington does publish a Regional Flood Exposure Model as a public VECTOR TILE service, but it is TilesOnly — renderable on a map, with no feature query and no attributes you can read. Tiles I sampled over central Wellington came back empty, so coverage looks limited to flood-prone areas. For queryable regional flood extent use flood-hazard-areas.

river-levels-viewer.note: The spreadsheet links a Web AppBuilder viewer. Its network calls show the real service: gauged flow sites, whose Name field matches Hilltop site names exactly (47/47), so this layer gives you the map pins and Hilltop gives you the readings.

coordinate_check.method: Coordinates cross-checked against two independent sources: Hilltop's own published lat/long for the same site names, and Esri's GeometryServer reprojecting the layers' raw NZTM Easting/Northing attributes.
coordinate_check.arcgis_vs_hilltop: 47/47 flow + 2/2 rainfall sites matched by name; median 0.4 m, 46/47 within 10 m
coordinate_check.reprojection_check: 12 sites reprojected independently from NZTM; max disagreement 0.59 m
coordinate_check.outlier: 'Waikanae River at Water Treatment Plant' - ArcGIS and Hilltop disagree by 228 m. Every other site agrees within 10 m, so this looks like one stale record rather than a systemic problem. Prefer the Hilltop coordinate, or treat that gauge's position as approximate.

rainfall-observations.note: The spreadsheet links one hard-coded Berhampore graph. The viewer actually loads a Rainfall map service. Layer 1 is time-filtered and is often empty; layer 2 carries the sites reporting rain in the last 6 hours. Names match Hilltop site names exactly, so join on Name for the values.

layers.0: Rainfall sites - no rainfall in last 6 hours

coordinate_check.method: Coordinates cross-checked against two independent sources: Hilltop's own published lat/long for the same site names, and Esri's GeometryServer reprojecting the layers' raw NZTM Easting/Northing attributes.
coordinate_check.arcgis_vs_hilltop: 47/47 flow + 2/2 rainfall sites matched by name; median 0.4 m, 46/47 within 10 m
coordinate_check.reprojection_check: 12 sites reprojected independently from NZTM; max disagreement 0.59 m
coordinate_check.outlier: 'Waikanae River at Water Treatment Plant' - ArcGIS and Hilltop disagree by 228 m. Every other site agrees within 10 m, so this looks like one stale record rather than a systemic problem. Prefer the Hilltop coordinate, or treat that gauge's position as approximate.

riskscape-coastal.note: This spreadsheet row is a service description, not a dataset - the title is copied from NIWA's consultancy page and the 'PCE, 2022' attribution looks wrong (the PCE coastal work is 2015 and its NIWA exposure annex is a PDF of tables only). RiskScape is software: no public model library, sample data or API, and the RiskScape folder on gis.niwa.co.nz publishes nothing anonymously. The exposure/loss outputs are not published as data anywhere. Use extra.niwa_coastal_flood instead - the national 1% AEP coastal flood hazard layer these overlays are run against, which IS public. Note that is the hazard extent, not the exposure result. Remaining AEP scenarios and flood-depth rasters are sold on NIWA's DataHub storefront.

nz-searise.note: Reachable after all. The Takiwa portal's API is effectively public: POST /api/users/loginAsGuest with an empty body issues a 20-minute guest session to anyone, no credentials, and every endpoint the map uses accepts it. The coastal site layer - 8,173 points at ~2 km spacing, each carrying vertical land movement rate, uncertainty, observation count and quality factor - comes down as one 3.6 MB GeoJSON from two zoom-3 tiles. Per-site projections give p17/p50/p83 sea-level rise in metres at 30 year-steps from 2005 to 2300, across 5 SSP scenarios with and without VLM. There is no bulk CSV or NetCDF anywhere - not on searise.nz, not on CKAN - so this API is the only programmatic route. BETTER ROUTE: NIWA also hosts the projection lookup table openly as an ArcGIS table — SLRprojectionTable_varispacing, 173,760 rows keyed by SSP (1-5), Year (1995-2150), Base_year (1995/2005/2020) and VLM (-9 to +9 mm/yr in 0.1 steps), returning RSLR in metres. Take a site's vertical land movement rate from the coastal sites layer, round to 0.1, and look up its projection — no guest token, no 4.5-hour scrape.
nz-searise.auth: POST https://searise.takiwa.co/api/users/loginAsGuest (empty body). Returns sessionKey (send as X-Session-Key header) and geotilesToken (send as ?geotilesToken= query param). Both expire after 20 minutes. You must carry the response cookies AND the header - either alone fails.
nz-searise.sites_geojson: https://geotiles.takiwa.co/geojson/tiles/sea_rise_national_with_vlm_sites_2024/3/{x}/{y}?options=%7B%22limit%22%3A0%7D&geotilesToken=<token> - the whole country is tiles 3/7/4 and 3/7/5
nz-searise.join: site ids from /api/datasetStructure/readGeodataSiteOptions join 1:1 to the GeoJSON 'name'
nz-searise.attribution: NZ SeaRise / Te Tai Pari O Aotearoa (ARC, GNS Science, NIWA), 2024 revision
nz-searise.gotchas: Needs a browser User-Agent (Cloudflare 403s the python-urllib default). A full national projection pull is ~140 MB and ~4.5 hours - server-side latency, not improved by parallelism - so CACHE IT, do not fetch live. A Wellington subset of 260 sites takes under 10 minutes. This is an undocumented internal API: be considerate with request rates, and expect it to change without notice.

groundwater-monitoring.note: The ArcGIS service the viewer loads is a token-gated copy and is a red herring. The viewer's own public config points at a completely open GeoServer WFS carrying the same layer: 206 monitoring bores nationally, 22 in Greater Wellington, already in WGS84, no key or cookie needed. Measured hydrochemistry is a separate anonymous CSV export (7,828 NGMP sample rows across 47 bores, current to May 2026) - join to the WFS on bore name (WFS 'Name' = CSV 'Feature'). Only 47 of the 206 bores carry public chemistry, 10 of them in Wellington. NGMP is CC BY 4.0, a carve-out from GGW's otherwise restrictive terms; cite DOI 10.21420/9QTA-4884. This is WFS, not ArcGIS REST, so wcc_gis cannot query it - use the URL directly.
groundwater-monitoring.caveat: GGW's server-side filtering needs a login, so the CSV is a fixed public extract rather than a query endpoint - filter client-side after download.

soil-classification-regional.note: The spreadsheet had no link at all. Greater Wellington publishes it: 4,719 soil polygons with full New Zealand Soil Classification attributes — NZSC and DOMNZSC codes, series, soil type, survey and phase. Anonymous, and outSR=4326 works. This is better than the Manaaki Whenua LRIS route, which needs an API key.
soil-classification-regional.found_via: GWRC ArcGIS org search, 2026-08-03; verified 4,719 features

coastal-hinterland.note: The NIWA MapServer for this publishes zero layers. But the hinterland classification is not a separate dataset at all — it is the HINTERLAND column on the Coastal Sensitivity Index service (7 classes: ler, lpdry, lpw, rg, sca, scf, vrpa), across the same 1,811 coastline segments. Query that service and read HINTERLAND alongside SHORE_TYPE, EXPOSURE and FS.
coastal-hinterland.found_via: field inspection of the CSI service, 2026-08-03

gw_hilltop.name: Greater Wellington Hilltop telemetry (river level, flow, rainfall)
gw_hilltop.why: The only genuinely real-time regional feed - 5-minute observations, current to the minute. Not in the spreadsheet, but the most useful thing for a live emergency picture.
gw_hilltop.coordinates: WGS84 lat/long directly - no reprojection needed
gw_hilltop.gotcha: Spaces in site names must be percent-encoded as %20. A '+' is NOT decoded server-side and returns 'No data for site'. The same server also answers on /data.hts; it is an alias, not a second dataset — both return the identical 3,340 sites and 70 measurements per site, so there is nothing extra to fetch there.

niwa_coastal_flood.name: NZ 1% AEP extreme sea-level flooding (NIWA, Paulik et al. 2023)
niwa_coastal_flood.why: Not in the spreadsheet, and the best coastal-inundation layer available: 192,377 polygons covering 21 sea-level-rise scenarios from 0 to 200 cm in 10 cm steps, filterable by region. This is the national hazard layer that coastal exposure studies are run against.
niwa_coastal_flood.licence: CC BY-ND 4.0, NIWA 2023. Cite Paulik et al. (2023) doi:10.3389/fenvs.2022.1045743

fields.SLR: sea-level rise in cm, 0-200 in 10 cm steps

niwa_coastal_flood.gotcha: Do NOT use the Hub bulk download - the national GeoJSON exceeds 2 GB. Always filter with a where clause on SLR/REGC2023 plus a bounding box. Bay of Plenty is excluded from the national service and lives in its own.

em_hackathon_bundle.name: EM Impact Labs hackathon layer bundles (WCC + GWRC)
em_hackathon_bundle.why: WCC published a purpose-built bundle for the hackathon itself: 24 layers (soil, wind zones, tsunami evacuation, fault traces, liquefaction, coastal and stream inundation, overland flowpaths, transport) on one FeatureServer, plus a companion GW_Layers service with 6 GWRC hazard layers. Largely overlaps the datasets already in this catalogue, but it is the officially-blessed stack in one call.

nema_cap_alerts.name: NEMA Emergency Mobile Alert history (CAP polygons)
nema_cap_alerts.why: Every Emergency Mobile Alert broadcast in NZ — live and historic — with the actual cell-broadcast target polygon. The authoritative 'has an official alert been issued over this area' layer. 108 records at verification: NEMA tsunami alerts, FENZ stay-inside notices, regional CDEM alerts. This is the feed behind the public map on getready.govt.nz, which itself blocks scripted clients.
nema_cap_alerts.gotcha: Live and historic records share the layer — filter on the 'historic' field. The same NEMA org also serves CDEM_Group_Boundaries (which CDEM group owns any point) and national tsunami-evacuation-zone vector tiles.

nema_electricity_outages.name: NEMA national electricity outages (BETA)
nema_electricity_outages.why: Near-real-time power outages aggregated across 18 lines companies — including Wellington Electricity and Powerco — with customer counts, planned/unplanned flags and restoration ETAs. One call gets the national picture; 94 live outages at verification, including a live Wellington Electricity job at Makara.

wellington_electricity_outages.name: Wellington Electricity outages (direct JSON)
wellington_electricity_outages.why: The distributor's own feed for Wellington City, Hutt Valley and Porirua: unplanned and planned outages with per-street coordinates, customers affected and ETA. Higher resolution than the NEMA aggregation for the target area.
wellington_electricity_outages.gotcha: The domain is welectricity.co.nz — wellingtonelectricity.co.nz does not resolve. A companion route /outages/getlvoutagedata is a property-level GeoJSON layer WEL switches on during major events; poll it, it is the high-resolution feed. Also: the response body is JSON but the server labels it Content-Type: text/html — requests.json() copes, a strict content-type check does not.

wellington_water_faults.name: Wellington Water live faults (Job Status Public View)
wellington_water_faults.why: 1,509 open water/wastewater/stormwater jobs (876 in Wellington City at verification) fed near-real-time from Wellington Water's Maximo works system, with addresses, priorities and status descriptions.
wellington_water_faults.gotcha: The live layer is index 5, not 0. Two similarly named layers on the same org — Water_Outage_(View) and Drinking_Water_Notice_(View) — are dead (0 records since 2018-19); do not use them. Wellington Water's website is now tiakiwai.co.nz.

community_emergency_hubs.name: Community Emergency Hubs + emergency facilities (GWRC/WREMO)
community_emergency_hubs.why: The WREMO hub network — 126 hubs region-wide, 36 in Wellington City — where communities coordinate after a disaster. The same Emergencies_P service also carries hospitals (13), medical centres (61), fire stations (32), police stations (11) and ambulance stations (5) on layers 1-6. Layers 7-24 are the hazard layers already in this catalogue.
community_emergency_hubs.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 — the one restrictive licence here; fine for a hackathon, flag before productising
community_emergency_hubs.gotcha: Paginate — the layer sets exceededTransferLimit at default page size. Facility metadata is a few years stale (pre-2022 DHB names) though geometry is sound. An Upper Hutt copy (services1.arcgis.com/H0o1MSouS8mlA3T1 → Community_Emergency_Hubs_in_Wellington, 127 hubs) carries a Link field of per-hub guide PDFs, but those URLs now 404 — WREMO consolidated them into one regional hub guide: https://www.wremo.nz/assets/Hub-Guides/Regional-Hub-Guide-2025/Wellington-Region-Hub-Guide-July-2025.pdf

wcc_emergency_water_tanks.name: WCC emergency water tanks
wcc_emergency_water_tanks.why: 45 emergency water storage tanks across Wellington City with owner, status, type and capacity in litres. Litres-per-suburb against population is a directly presentable resilience metric. Companions on the Wellington Water org: 21 community water stations and 37 alternative abstraction points (both static 2019 reference layers).

wcc_emergency_routes.name: WCC emergency routes (post-disaster road reopening stages)
wcc_emergency_routes.why: 429 road segments carrying wccReopStg — the staged order WCC plans to reopen roads after a major earthquake. Overlay against liquefaction and landslide layers to see which reopening stages are at risk. The most operationally specific Wellington layer found.
wcc_emergency_routes.licence: Service metadata says 'Please consult WCC prior to use' — email before shipping anything public

geonet_api.name: GeoNet APIs (quakes, CAP alerts, intensity, strong motion, volcano)
geonet_api.why: The primary 'what just happened' feeds: earthquake catalogue seconds after detection, CAP-format alerts, measured vs crowdsourced felt intensity, per-station PGA/PGV (173 strong-motion stations in the Wellington bbox), volcano alert levels and GNS news bulletins.
geonet_api.gotcha: Quake records include quality='deleted' retractions inline in the feed — filter them out. The old FITS API is decommissioned; time-series data now lives on Tilde (see geonet_tilde).

geonet_tilde.name: GeoNet Tilde — Wellington Harbour tsunami gauge, DART buoys, GNSS
geonet_tilde.why: Sea level in Wellington Harbour (station WLGT, in the CBD) at 15-second cadence. The water-height-detided series has the astronomical tide already removed, so thresholding the residual IS a tsunami / storm-surge detector — no harmonic modelling needed. The dart domain adds 12 deep-ocean buoys spanning the Hikurangi-Kermadec arc (an hour of distant-source lead time), and gnss daily displacement at WGTN shows slow-slip transients.
geonet_tilde.gotcha: DART sensor codes rotate on every buoy redeployment — read dataSummary and pick the code with the newest latestRecord, never hardcode. NZA (offshore Wellington) was stale at verification; use NZB/NZC. Cross-check gauge readings against UNESCO IOC (ioc-sealevelmonitoring.org, station code wlgt, 1-minute) — NZ stations there are keyed country='NWZ'.

gns_fault_avoidance_zones.name: GNS NZ Active Fault Datasets (fault avoidance zones, slip rates)
gns_fault_avoidance_zones.why: Planning-grade fault data far richer than the 1:250k traces in this catalogue's active-faults: recurrence interval, slip rate, last event, single-event displacement, high-resolution traces, Fault Avoidance Zones and Fault Awareness Areas. Layer 7 (avoidance zones) returned 56 features over the Wellington bbox — Wellington, Ohariu, Moonshine, Shepherds Gully, Terawhiti and Whitemans Valley faults. 'Is this address in a fault avoidance zone' mirrors how councils regulate consents.
gns_fault_avoidance_zones.gotcha: On the same server, the Landslides, LandslideResponse and NZAFD folders are empty — live content is under Active_Faults and EILD.

gns_eild.name: GNS EILD — earthquake-induced landslide probability
gns_eild.why: Coseismic landslide probability rasters at 100/250/500/1000-year PGA return periods: after a quake, which slopes are likely to fail. The cascading-hazard dimension the catalogue's static landslide layers do not model. Same folder also holds the NZ Landslide Dam Database (outburst-flood secondary hazard).
gns_eild.gotcha: Raster layers — use /export for images and /identify for per-point values. The 32 m and 256 m rasters return NoData at the Wellington CBD; the 512 m layer has coverage. Probe multiple resolutions per point.

fenz_operational.name: FENZ live fires, permits and fire season status
fenz_operational.why: The service behind checkitsalright.nz: active vegetation fires (17 at verification), approved burn permits (2,597 — a fire-risk proxy), and fire-season status polygons. The companion JSON API resolves any point to its nearest fire-weather station and daily danger rating. FENZ also publishes eight years of national incident CSVs (CC-BY 4.0) on data.govt.nz for demand baselines.
fenz_operational.gotcha: fireandemergency.nz/incidents is Incapsula-blocked to scripts — this ArcGIS service is the working route. Fire-danger risk-index payloads were empty in winter; shape unverified until fire season.

metlink_gtfs.name: Metlink public transport (GTFS + realtime)
metlink_gtfs.why: The complete bus/train/ferry network graph — routes, stops, timetables, shapes — as one keyless zip, refreshed roughly weekly. The offline evacuation-routing backbone. Realtime vehicle positions, trip updates and service alerts exist on the API host with a free self-service key.
metlink_gtfs.auth: none for static GTFS; realtime (api.opendata.metlink.org.nz/v1/gtfs-rt/*) needs a free key from opendata.metlink.org.nz — register before the event

nz_deprivation_2023.name: NZ Index of Deprivation 2023 (NZDep2023) by small area
nz_deprivation_2023.why: The catalogue can say where the tsunami zone is but nothing about who lives in it. NZDep2023 is the standard small-area measure of socioeconomic deprivation, and deprivation decile is the usual proxy for who cannot self-evacuate, lacks transport, or needs checking on first. 32,746 SA1 polygons nationally; 1,936 intersect the Wellington City bounding box.
nz_deprivation_2023.licence: Not stated on the service. Underlying NZDep2023 is University of Otago work published with Stats NZ geographies — check before republishing.
nz_deprivation_2023.found_via: cyclone.api and thecolab-ai/.skills sweep; independently verified 2026-08-04

nzta_traffic_cameras.name: NZTA live traffic cameras and delays
nzta_traffic_cameras.why: 319 state-highway cameras nationally, about 42 around the Wellington region, each with a live JPEG URL — the thing an operations room actually looks at. The catalogue already has NZTA warnings; this is the picture behind them. A companion delays feed carries 144 current entries.
nzta_traffic_cameras.gotcha: Check Offline and UnderMaintenance before showing an image — a camera that is down still appears in the feed. Images are fetched straight from trafficnz.info/camera/<id>.jpg.
nzta_traffic_cameras.found_via: cyclone.api and thecolab-ai/.skills sweep; independently verified 2026-08-04

telco_outages.name: Mobile network outages (2degrees, One NZ)
telco_outages.why: Comms failure is a first-order emergency concern and nothing else in the catalogue covers it. 2degrees publishes planned and unplanned outages as plain JSON with location and affected area.
telco_outages.gotcha: One NZ publishes only a config file keylessly (one.nz/getconfigvalues/outage-config.json, itself JSON mislabelled as text/html); its actual outage list sits behind a GraphQL POST and is not a simple GET. NEMA's national electricity outage feed covers power, not telco.
telco_outages.found_via: cyclone.api and thecolab-ai/.skills sweep; independently verified 2026-08-04

civil_defence_ema_feed.name: Civil Defence Emergency Mobile Alert feed
civil_defence_ema_feed.why: The RSS feed of Emergency Mobile Alerts actually broadcast. Note that docs/additional-sources.md lists civildefence.govt.nz under dead ends — that is the main site; this alerthub subdomain responds.
civil_defence_ema_feed.gotcha: Empty between events — it carried no items when checked, which is the normal state. Test your parser against nema_cap_alerts, which has the broadcast polygons and current content.
civil_defence_ema_feed.found_via: cyclone.api and thecolab-ai/.skills sweep; independently verified 2026-08-04
